summary: Closeout can read SHA evidence from a sibling branch and can hide open work under a deferred [b] parent. The committed suites pass.
blocking_findings: F1 [Blocker] review-a: measure_interphase_checks.py:1150 can select an earlier sibling instead of an ancestor when it skips ignored boxes. With a SHA'd [x] root, a deferred [ ] child, and an ignored [ ] sibling with a SHA-less [x] child, closeout incorrectly reports a missing SHA. An earlier sibling branch with its own SHA can also hide a real missing-SHA diagnostic under an uncovered root. Restrict the SHA lookup to active ancestors and test both results.

F2 [Blocker] review-a: measure_interphase_checks.py:1113 skips the standard [b] marker. If a SHA'd [x] task precedes a deferred [b] task, the deferred task's open child inherits the ignore from the previous task. A fixture with `- [b] Pending review a1b2c3d deferred:owner` and one indented open child made role-gate closeout exit 0 at HEAD, versus exit 1 at the base. Retain the deferred box as a boundary for the ignore and test the caller result.
nonblocking_findings: F3 [Nit] review-a: test_closeout_nested_subboxes.py:136 does not isolate a nested [x] box's own SHA. A mutant that discards an [x] box's own SHA under an ignored parent passes all 18 cases. Give case 09 a SHA-less root and expect only the root's missing-SHA diagnostic.

F4 [Nit] review-a: CHANGELOG.md:49 still says that only top-level tasks require a SHA. Case 11 shows that a nested [x] box also needs its own SHA when it has no covered ancestor. State that a nested [x] box can inherit coverage.
evidence: HEAD and the role base resolved to be0db155df52526e789ffcca83f9cffc2f855cbe. The checkout was clean and git diff --check passed for a943347..be0db15.
The active plan has no separate test-strategy.md. The light-lane plan lists the test command and the three tasks. The audit read the spec review, the role logs, and the contracts.

build-graph indexes TypeScript, not the changed Python function. git grep found the two direct callers at measure_interphase_checks.py:464 and :1210. The status command, closeout command, and closeout role gate use those callers.

The phase diff changes only plan_closeout_feedback in the checker. The base and HEAD return the same phase_counts, jr_green_phase_counts, and track_incomplete values for the caller fixtures. The final-acceptance branch has no call to plan_closeout_feedback.
The real Math lines 38–50 give no feedback. Lines 52–60 give only the missing SHA for line 52. An independent active-ancestor scan matches all 102 diagnostics on the full plan.
The full Math plan retains 15 top-level and 56 nested missing-SHA lines. It also retains 5 top-level open lines and 26 nested open lines under open parents. The base gave 302 lines.
A3: the new tests assert exact messages, a fixed candidate list, or the numeric track_incomplete result. They do not look for bare digits in output.

A4: a fixture without an archived plan returns no candidate and role-gate closeout exits 1 with the missing-plan diagnostic. A valid nested-open fixture changes from exit 1 to exit 0, but the top-level-open control remains at exit 1.
